events.h: eThekwini council will reconvene on Friday to elect a mayor and speaker
events.dek: eThekwini’s inaugural council meeting adjourned on 24 November without electing a mayor, deputy mayor or speaker, and IOL reports the council will reconvene on Friday to do so. IOL and Briefly News report the ANC and MK have reached an eThekwini agreement, though the parties were coy at the sitting.
brief: Several outlets report the council adjourned without filling a leadership position to allow coalition talks to conclude; IOL reports it reconvenes on Friday to elect a mayor and speaker.
Central News South Africa reports the EFF welcomed the adjournment, and DailyNews reports ActionSA rejected DA pressure over the eThekwini coalition.
eNCA reports the sitting went ahead despite a KwaZulu-Natal Cogta directive to delay it, which DailyNews and the Sunday Tribune report the city manager challenged.
IOL reports the ANC and MK sealed an eThekwini deal and Briefly News reports an agreement was reportedly reached; EWN reports the parties were coy at the sitting.
The MK Party says its mayoral candidate has an “unblemished record”, IOL and The Mercury report.

events.h: Faku returns in Buffalo City with the EFF as a DA-led coalition signs for Nelson Mandela Bay
events.dek: Princess Faku was re-elected Buffalo City mayor, beating the UDM’s Nqabayomzi Kwankwa, and BusinessTech reports the ANC teamed up with the EFF. In Nelson Mandela Bay, a DA-led multiparty coalition has been formed, but News24 reports an ANC-led filibuster blocked the vote for mayor and speaker.
brief: eNCA, EWN and Briefly News report Faku was re-elected; Briefly News says she defeated the UDM’s Nqabayomzi Kwankwa, and BusinessTech says the ANC is running the metro with the EFF.
News24 reports ANC divisions over Faku’s return, quoting one voice saying “you cannot smuggle her back”.

News24 says the DA will govern Nelson Mandela Bay with the FF Plus, UDM, ActionSA and PAC; several outlets report a six-party deal, SABC News reports a four-party DA-led coalition, and HeraldLIVE says Retief Odendaal is set to be mayor.

News24 reports the DA’s plan to elect a mayor and speaker was blocked by an ANC-led filibuster, The National reports there is no mayor yet, and Daily Maverick says the ANC scrambled for a last-minute coalition.
HeraldLIVE reports a 'black caucus' insists the Nelson Mandela Bay coalition is not a done deal.

events.h: Malema awaits judgment in his bid to gag Zille over her Joburg claims
events.dek: EFF leader Julius Malema went to court to stop DA mayoral candidate Helen Zille repeating claims about him, in a dispute linked to the Johannesburg coalition fight, and the court reserved judgment. Zille refused to retract, and Briefly News reports ActionSA’s Michael Beaumont shared a 2016 email he says contradicts her claims.

News24 reports Zille fought the gag bid using Malema’s own words, including 'we were controlling him'.
IOL reports the court reserved judgment, and eNCA reports Malema is awaiting the outcome.

events.h: Ekurhuleni’s mayoral election moves to Friday as parties wait on the ANC to sign
events.dek: Ekurhuleni’s new council held its inaugural meeting on 25 November, but the election of a mayor and speaker was postponed, and SABC News, The National and Inside Metros report the vote will take place on Friday. EWN, The National and Sunday World report parties are waiting on the ANC to sign off the coalition deal, while IOL reports the DA is still pursuing a deal as ANC-ActionSA talks continue.
brief: The Citizen, EWN, IOL, News24, Briefly News and Business Day report the mayoral election was postponed so coalition partners could finish negotiations; SABC News, The National and Inside Metros report the vote moves to Friday.

events.h: The ANC leaves coalition choices to its provinces and regions
events.dek: EWN and Dan Corder report the ANC’s NEC has let provinces and regions decide coalitions, with consequences for Gauteng, eThekwini, Nelson Mandela Bay and over 100 hung councils, and SABC News reports the NEC resolved that DA coalitions should be a last resort. The ANC says there is consensus as talks move towards conclusion, while TimesLIVE and IOL report strains over Ramaphosa’s leadership and The Common Sense reports the SACP calling a Sol Plaatje deal with the DA a “betrayal”.
brief: EWN asks whether the ANC has given provinces and regions the final say; Dan Corder says the NEC decided to let regional bodies choose, affecting well over 100 hung councils.
SABC News reports the NEC resolved that coalitions with the DA should be a 'last resort'.
Newsnote reports the ANC asserting there is consensus as talks near conclusion; The Witness reports the NEC weighing up its coalition future.

Business Day reports the ANC is seeking a foothold in hung councils, EWN quotes an analyst saying its choices could decide whether it enters a 'death spiral', and IOL reports the SACP drawing a line over coalition support for the ANC.
The Common Sense reports the SACP called the ANC’s handling of a DA deal in Sol Plaatje a “betrayal”.

TimesLIVE reports Ramaphosa faces a tough ANC unity test, IOL reports tensions over Ramaphosa, election losses and working with the DA, and The Common Sense argues ANC indecision has left a power vacuum.
